customManagers.description: Dockerfile ARG version pins (github-releases / github-tags / pypi) with a `# renovate:` marker on the line above -- the Dockerfile is the single source of truth for every component version (ci/read_pins.py)
Docker base images in ARGs: `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=<image> ...` above `ARG X=<image>:<tag>[@digest]`
libr4d: a raw commit SHA on Codeberg main, tracked as a git-refs digest (R4D_REPO must stay in sync with depName)
Tool versions in workflow env blocks (`# renovate:` marker above `NAME: value`)

packageRules.description: setup-python pins the image's interpreter (the venv is Ubuntu 24.04's python 3.12; ci/check_constraints.py evaluates markers for it) -- it moves with the release base, not on its own
PyTorch stack moves together (torch / triton / torchvision pins are a tested trio, see the Dockerfile comment)
prBodyNotes: Tested trio: bump torch, triton and torchvision together. Patch anchors: patch_gfx1201 (triton driver.py), patch_dynamo_metrics (torch/_dynamo/utils.py) -- CI patch-dryrun must stay green, then a full builder-stage rebuild (hours) and an A/B on the GPU before the image goes to production.

packageRules.description: vLLM: every bump needs the patch dry run, a build and an A/B on the GPU
prBodyNotes: Most patches anchor on vLLM source (see the Dockerfile loop). Expect anchor drift on minor bumps: fix the patches in the same PR, keep CI patch-dryrun green, then build.yml + A/B (func_check, BetterBench, GSM8K gate) before rollout. sly/radiance_attn_drafter rebinds triton_attn.unified_attention and launches triton_unified_attention.kernel_unified_attention / reduce_segments by keyword: run sly/check_attn_drafter.py, check the start log for `drafter attn plan:` (the accept gate requires it) and re-run sly/bench_drafter_attn.py --check on the card. sly/radiance_lookup_draft wraps the V2 runner: GPUModelRunner.__init__ (speculator, req_states), DFlash2Speculator.propose (draft_tokens, draft_logits, _cached_candidate_ids, selector_top_k), req_states.all_token_ids / total_len and the rejection sampler's draft_logits contract: run sly/check_lookup_draft.py and, on the card, sly/bench_lookup_draft.py --check --rejection (the accept gate requires the `lookup draft: installed` marker).

packageRules.description: aiter: patch_unified_attention_lds / patch_radiance_dispatch / sly/patch_quark_mxfp4 anchor on it; sly/radiance_attn_decode wraps its unified-attention config API
prBodyNotes: aiter is compiled from source in the builder stage; anchors in patch_unified_attention_lds, patch_radiance_dispatch and sly/patch_quark_mxfp4 plus sly/mxfp4-configs need re-verification. sly/radiance_attn_decode wraps get_unified_attention_config / use_2d_kernel and reads the _UAParams fields: run sly/check_attn_decode.py, check the start log for `decode attn tune installed` (the accept gate requires it), and re-run sly/bench_decode_attn.py --table if the attention tables or kernels changed.

packageRules.description: ROCm base image: major/minor is a toolchain change (new hipcc, new compile cache key); keep as its own PR
prBodyNotes: A ROCm bump rebuilds every stage (cold build, hours) and invalidates the torch.compile / AOT caches on the GPU host (double start on rollout). Pin the same major.minor in the image tag (build.yml derives rocmX.Y from ROCM_BASE).

packageRules.description: Release base: Ubuntu release must match the ROCm base (venv python 3.12) -- digest updates only (docker datasource only: the `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` runner pins are github-runners and get their PRs, see the GitHub Actions rule)
rocm_bandwidth_test: rocm-7.x tags need the new cmake framework (clang>=19, vendored submodules) -- stay on 6.x

GitHub Actions in one PR -- this also covers the pinned runner images in `runs-on:` (github-runners datasource), which is why they are pinned to `ubuntu-24.04` instead of riding `ubuntu-latest`: a runner image change is a toolchain change and belongs in a PR that CI can fail on, not in a label that flips on a date
CI lint tools in one PR

Image Python dependencies (constraints.txt): one weekly PR for all minor/patch updates (renovate/python-deps) and one for the majors (renovate/major-python-deps, Renovate's default major split). Each PR is checked by ci/check_constraints.py (the pins must be exactly what pip resolves for the pinned vLLM); the image itself is built by build.yml after merge + VERSION bump
prBodyNotes: Pins in constraints.txt. CI `constraints` job: `python3 ci/check_constraints.py` must be green (a failure names the vLLM range the bump leaves, or a new/obsolete transitive dependency -- add an `allowedVersions` rule in renovate.json or fix the file). Changes the image's cold venv layer: the next release is a full ~750 MB venv download once. Merge, then bump VERSION for build.yml + the acceptance gate.
